items.title: New World Development bags Shanghai bourse nod for US$570mil REIT listing
items.summary: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's New World Development said on Monday the Shanghai Stock Exchange had approved the spinoff and listing of its REIT for an expected offering size of 3.82 billion yuan (US$570.36 million). * As part of the transaction, New World will sell the holding company of Shanghai Hong Kong New World Tower to the newly listed REIT for 4.01 billion yuan. * The REIT listing comes as New World seeks to refinance debt ⁠and bolster liquidity amid weakness in Hong Kong's property sector.

items.title: Hong Kong brands use Malaysia as springboard into Asean e-commerce
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong companies are turning to Malaysia as a test market for expanding across Southeast Asia, using the country's growing e-commerce ecosystem to reach consumers without the upfront costs of building a physical retail presence. About 100 Hong Kong brands are taking part in the inaugural Hong Kong Shopping Festival in Malaysia, offering more than 350 products as the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) seeks to deepen commercial links with the region. HKTDC regional director, Southeast Asia & South Asia, Leung Kwan Ho, said the festival was intended to bring Hong Kong products closer to Malaysian consumers while helping participating companies explore new markets.

items.title: Freediving offers quieter, low-impact way to explore ocean, says expert
items.summary: SEMPORNA: Freediving offers a quieter, lower-impact way to explore the ocean, allowing divers to minimise disturbance to marine life, says the Philippines' top-ranked freediver Maria Noella Zosa. "Unlike scuba diving, freedivers can control their movements and reduce bubbles underwater. Bubbles interfere with marine life.

items.title: Melaka polls: 'Just tell us if you're not interested', says Amirudin
items.summary: MASJID TANAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) wants Barisan Nasional (BN) to clarify its stance on possible cooperation in the upcoming Melaka election as there has been no progress on talks between the two sides. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said PH had no issue if BN was not interested in working together but wanted a clear decision so it could proceed with preparations for the polls. "Initially, they said they might go solo, then they said they might go with Pas, and after that, they could also go with PH.

items.title: Kedah PKR says Umno dissolution push serves political interests, not urgent need for stability
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 21 — Kedah Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) maintains that there is no urgent need to dissolve Parliament, as called for by Kedah Umno Strategic Communications director Syed Mohd Johan Rizal Syed Unan Mashri. State Leadership Council (MPN) Communications director Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said the call clearly did not stem from any pressing need, but rather served Umno’s political interests. He said the call also contradicted the position of Umno president, who had only recently reaffirmed that Umno would remain with the Unity Government until the end of its term.

items.title: Rosmah: Now I know who our true friends are
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor said the response to her husband’s situation has shown her who has stood by the family “through difficult and good times”, as well-wishers at home and abroad offer to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. In a statement last night, Rosmah said she was touched, and that the support had not come only from friends and acquaintances in Malaysia. That is all,” she said.

items.title: Serian again tops unhealthy API readings at 168
items.summary: In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded an API reading of 153, while Kota Kinabalu recorded 133. Another 38 areas recorded moderate API readings. Labuan recorded 93.

items.title: UK property asking prices rise for first time since May
items.summary: LONDON: British property sellers have increased the prices they want for their homes for the first time since May, real estate website Rightmove said on Monday. Prices for property put up for sale rose by 0.7 per cent between Aug 9 and Sept 12, a slightly bigger monthly increase than average for the time of year and following a drop of two per cent in the preceding four weeks, it said. Rightmove also said: * Asking ⁠prices were 0.8 per cent lower than a year earlier, after a 1.0 per cent annual drop in Rightmove's August report * The number of homes available to purchase hit a 12-year high * The number of buyer enquiries was 9.0 per cent lower than this time last year * "September's above-average price rise is a welcome sign of confidence after a particularly subdued summer, but it should be viewed as a modest recovery," Colleen Babcock, property expert at Rightmove said.

items.title: Police confirm Tambun fire victims died from injuries and smoke inhalation after post‑mortems
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — Post-mortems on the three victims of a fire at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun, here yesterday found that two of them died from fire-related injuries. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said another victim died from smoke inhalation. Three family members, comprising an elderly couple and their grandson, died in the incident.

items.title: #NSTviral: 'Take your rubbish with you': Beach cleanup videos strike a chord online
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man's frustration over rubbish along the coast of Pulau Redang, Terengganu, has struck a chord with social media users after he posted videos of himself cleaning up the waste. Threads user @jacksonlim_0815 questioned why people continued to discard rubbish indiscriminately, pointing out that waste could end up in the sea and wash ashore. "Why do so many people throw rubbish everywhere?"

items.title: Anwar: Royal institution fails if it can be changed indiscriminately
items.summary: "In Negri Sembilan, those who make a lot of noise about the Malay Rulers, Malay Rulers, Malay Rulers, but when a decision does not go their way, they want to remove that Malay Ruler... We follow the Constitution and law. The Ruler must follow the Constitution.

items.title: Ringgit opens mixed against major, Asean currencies after BOJ rate hike
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened mixed against major and Asean currencies on Monday as investors assessed the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) rate hike on Friday. Meanwhile, the local note opened slightly lower against the US dollar today. At 8am, the ringgit eased to 4.0810/0865 against the greenback from last Friday's close of 4.0795/0840.

items.title: Asean, US deepen trade ties with new 2026–2027 cooperation plan
items.summary: MANILA: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) and the United States (US) are deepening economic cooperation through a new two-year work plan aimed at strengthening trade and investment ties in key areas such as the digital economy, agriculture, trade facilitation and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported. The 2026–2027 Asean-US Trade and Investment Framework Arrangement (TIFA) Work Plan was endorsed during the Asean Economic Ministers-United States Trade Representative (AEM-USTR) Consultation in Manila on Sunday, co-chaired by Trade Secretary Ma. Cristina Roque and US deputy trade representative Ambassador Rick Switzer.

items.title: Fuel cost absorption seen having minimal impact on TNB earnings
items.summary: Analyst Max Koh said the allocation, estimated for the September to December period, would account for about two per cent to three per cent of RHB Research's financial year 2026 (FY26) earnings forecast for the utility company. "TNB said the exemption is necessary to shield 90 per cent of residential customers from higher fuel prices, as the number of 600-800kWh consumers had risen to constitute 20 per cent of total user volume in July from 13 per cent in January," Koh said in a note. Koh said TNB's share price had declined 12 per cent from its recent high, presenting an opportunity to accumulate the stock on price weakness.

items.title: Tech leads shares higher in Asia, oil eases
items.summary: Japan's Nikkei was shut but futures rose 0.5 per cent, while South Korea's tech-heavy index gained 1.1 per cent. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.3 per cent. S&P 500 futures firmed 0.3 per cent, while Nasdaq futures added 0.4 per cent.

items.title: Haze update: 21 areas across Malaysia at ‘Unhealthy’ pollution levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21: A total of 21 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8.30am today, according to the Department of Environment (DoE), with Sarawak accounting for more than half of the country's worst-hit areas. A cluster of four stations, namely Nilai in Negeri Sembilan alongside Miri, Bintulu, and Kuching in Sarawak, all tied close behind at 158. Sarawak heavily blanketed with 11 stations Sarawak remained overwhelmingly the most affected state, accounting for 11 of the 21 unhealthy stations recorded this morning.

items.title: Kelat remains in stable condition despite 100kg weight loss, says MPT
items.summary: IPOH: A viral photograph showing Kelat appearing unusually thin does not reflect the elephant's current condition, said the Taiping Municipal Council (MPT). It said Kelat remained in good and stable condition, was active and continued to cooperate during training sessions at Tennoji Zoo in Osaka, Japan. MPT said Tennoji Zoo was closely monitoring signs of Kelat's musth, including increasing secretions from his temporal glands.

items.title: South Korea Sept 1-20 exports hit record high
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea's exports for the first 20 days of this month hit a record on a surge in chip sales, customs data showed on Monday. Exports rose 78.3 per cent from a year earlier to US$71.4 billion, the highest 20-day performance on record, as semiconductor shipments increased 259.4 per cent. On average each working day, exports were up 89.8 per cent.

items.title: US Treasury chief says meeting with China on trade, AI 'very successful'
items.summary: NEW YORK: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent touted a "very successful" meeting on trade and artificial intelligence with Chinese officials Sunday, adding that both sides discussed greater communication on artificial intelligence (AI) threats. "We just had a very successful engagement with the Chinese on trade and AI," Bessent told reporters after the all-day meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of a high-stakes summit Thursday in Washington between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping. Regarding artificial intelligence, Bessent said the US has proposed "a notification mechanism between the two countries, and we want a shared vision of common goals and common threats."

items.title: Police tracking Proton Wira driver after Axia ends up in ditch on NSE
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down the driver of a Proton Wira following an incident in which a Perodua Axia lost control and ended up in a ditch along the North-South Expressway. He urged anyone with information on the Proton Wira or its driver to come forward and assist police. Hasbullah also reminded motorists against actions on the road that could endanger themselves or other road users.

items.title: Fed's Kashkari says US inflation remains too high
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. Kashkari supported the unanimous vote last week to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3.75-4.00 per cent. FED CHAIRMAN ECHOES INFLATION CONCERNS Kashkari's inflation concerns largely echoed those voiced by Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh after the conclusion of the latest rate-setting meeting on Wednesday.

items.title: When oil crosses US$100: Malaysia's inflation–fiscal trade-off
items.summary: Brent crude has again moved above US$100 a barrel, recently trading around US$106–107 and having touched approximately US$113.50. The immediate question for Malaysia is naturally whether such prices will produce another inflationary shock. Malaysia has considerable capacity to insulate households from international oil prices.

items.title: Series of explosions heard near Aleppo in northern Syria
items.summary: DAMASCUS: A powerful blast was heard near Aleppo in northern Syria early Monday, followed by a series of explosions, state media reported. Syrian state television said "a blast was heard in the Al-Eis area in the southern Aleppo countryside" and was being investigated. Aleppo civil defence operations chief Faisal Mohammad Ali, quoted by the state-run Al-Ikhbariya channel, said the "ongoing explosions" were hampering access to emergency services and warned civilians not to approach the area.

items.title: Malaysia's palm oil compass: Keep Europe, grow new markets
items.summary: Should Malaysia keep looking over its shoulder at Europe, or turn more confidently towards new markets? The answer is neither Europe first nor Europe free. Malaysia needs a portfolio strategy: protect valuable markets, develop new ones and ensure that no single destination gains too much influence over our national interest.

items.title: Coffee bean prices tumble, but will Malaysians pay less for their daily cup?
items.summary: This means green bean prices have fallen 21.49 per cent so far this year. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd, in its Sept 13 consumer sector note, said coffee prices had already fallen 18.6 per cent year-to-date (YTD) and 29.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to US$2.91 per pound as at Sept 10. Wheat climbed 42.8 per cent, tin 37.3 per cent, polyethylene 36.6 per cent, sugar 28.4 per cent and crude palm oil 16.4 per cent.

items.title: Haze winners and losers: Healthcare gains as airlines, tourism feel the heat
items.summary: Analysts see healthcare as the clearest potential beneficiary of a prolonged haze episode, alongside stronger demand for air purifiers, while airlines, tourism players and solar operators face the costs of dirtier skies. Renewable energy players could also see solar generation fall as haze blocks sunlight, although the immediate earnings impact is expected to be limited. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analysts said the impact is already showing up in healthcare data.

items.title: Oil rises after Houthi attack on Saudi capital
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices rose on Monday after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched missile and drone strikes at Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh on Saturday, escalating tension in the Middle East while the US and Iran remained in stalemate. Brent crude futures climbed 81 cents, or 0.78 per cent, to US$104.68 a barrel by 2202 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$101.06 a barrel, up 76 cents, or 0.76 per cent. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Traditional banks risk losing SME business as open finance takes hold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian banks risk losing a significant share of their small and medium enterprise (SME) business to financial technology (fintech) firms and challenger banks as open finance reshapes the financial landscape, a banking expert said. Manaf Gardner Associates co-founder and chief executive officer Colyn Gardner said the experience in the United Kingdom (UK) showed how quickly non-traditional financial providers could gain ground in areas long dominated by established banks. He said Malaysian banks should take heed, given the country's large SME sector.

items.title: ICE agent shoots man during foot pursuit in Austin
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot and wounded a man in Austin, Texas, on Sunday, city officials said, adding that the man was in serious but stable condition. The ICE agent shot him during a brief pursuit on foot shortly before 1 p.m. local time, Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis said. ICE recently started detaining more people in Austin, Watson and US Representative Greg Casar, a Texas Democrat, said.

items.title: Future fighter must match Malaysia's defence needs, not prestige
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) will base its future multi-role combat aircraft requirement on capabilities that match Malaysia's defence stance and operational needs, rather than simply pursuing the most advanced fighter technology available. RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the decision on the future fighter fleet must consider the country's defensive posture, which was primarily focused on defending its sovereignty and airspace "It must begin with a fundamental question: what capability does Malaysia require and what role does it need the aircraft to perform? Beyond the choice of aircraft, Norazlan said RMAF was also reassessing the traditional approach of determining fighter fleet size.

items.title: Smaller firms face uphill climb to RM3,000 minimum wage by 2030
items.summary: Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) adviser Datuk Shamsuddin Bardan said the road towards a RM3,000 minimum wage by 2030 would be especially challenging for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Shamsuddin said simply expecting employers to shoulder higher wages without addressing productivity would be difficult. Shamsuddin said companies, particularly smaller businesses, also need to replace outdated technology, something many struggle to afford.

items.title: RM12,000 RMAF innovation delivers nearly RM150m in potential savings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) has averted at least six potentially costly bird strike incidents involving its prized Su-30MKM fighter jets, saving nearly RM150 million in potential engine repair costs. "The modest air intake screen (AIS) modification, which costs RM12,000, was designed to address one of the greatest hazards faced by fighter aircraft during take-off and landing — sucking in foreign objects, such as stones, debris or birds. Norazlan said a fighter aircraft's engines generate tremendous suction during take-off as they draw in large volumes of air for combustion.

items.title: Iran FM to visit Qatar for talks before UN assembly
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was due for talks in Qatar, a key mediator in the US-Iran war, before travelling to New York to attend the United Nations General Assembly, state media reported Sunday. The minister "left Teheran on Sunday evening bound for New York... and will make a brief stop in Doha to hold consultations on the latest developments in the region," state news agency IRNA reported. The stop in Doha comes as Iranian officials say they have once again stated through mediators Teheran's conditions for ending its blockade of the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Evolving threats push RMAF to strengthen maritime watch
items.summary: Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris told the New Straits Times that the service must place greater emphasis on maintaining an aerial watch over the country's waters as maritime security challenges continued to evolve. "Malaysia's maritime security challenges today are increasingly complex and multifaceted. As a maritime nation, it depends heavily on sea lines of communication for trade, resource security and economic stability," he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan Ruler revokes exco appointments over breach of oath, orders MB to propose new line-up
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir has revoked the appointments of the state’s executive councillors with immediate effect, saying they breached their oath of office through their actions and statements on September 15. “His Royal Highness the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Darul Khusus has revoked the appointment of Members of the State Executive Council, Negeri Sembilan with immediate effect for violating their oath of office,” the statement said. Bernama reported that the state government had collectively decided that the proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz was valid.

items.title: Hotspots, peat fires and palm oil: Why tracing Malaysia’s haze is so complicated
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The return of the haze across parts of Malaysia has once again brought forest and land fires in the region into focus. Malaysia’s response this time includes an offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, which reflects the fact that the haze does not stop at national borders. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi on Thursday said Malaysia had offered a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force.

items.title: Anwar: Najib has right to seek pardon, but wider impact must be considered
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s right to seek a pardon, while cautioning that its impact on public confidence and international perceptions must also be weighed. Anwar also rejected suggestions that he had paved the way for Najib’s conditional pardon, saying every prisoner had the right to submit an appeal for consideration. “What I said is that every prisoner has the right to submit an appeal, and I stand by defending that right for anyone, including Datuk Seri Najib.

items.title: Anwar to meet Loke before deciding on resignation, says no letter submitted yet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will meet Transport Minister Anthony Loke to hear his views before deciding whether to accept his resignation. Anwar said Loke had informed him of his intention to step down following the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak but had yet to submit a formal resignation letter. Speaking to media in Shah Alam today, Anwar said he wanted to sit down with Loke before making any decision.

items.title: Childcare is economic infrastructure, not ‘just a job’, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The childcare profession should be regarded as an important component in supporting the family economy and not merely as a job involving the care of children, said the Prime Minister’s Senior Political Adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said having trusted childcare providers enabled parents to work with greater peace of mind while ensuring that their children received proper care, making the childcare sector part of the country’s economic and social support ecosystem. Since its launch in August 2025, Kasih Madani has reached more than 1,000 childcare providers in four states — Kuala Lumpur, Perak, Kedah and Penang — through programmes such as the Madani Childcare Pilot Course (KARISMA), Madani Childcare Seminar (SEMAI) and Madani Childcare Professionalisation Skills Mentoring (BITARA).

items.title: Fake cops scare retired Bachok teacher into handing over ATM cards and wife’s gold necklace
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — A 75-year-old retired teacher in Bachok lost about RM15,000 after being duped by a scam syndicate posing as police officers, which also resulted in the victim handing over two ATM cards and his wife’s gold necklace with a pendant. Kelantan Police Chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said that the police arrested a 31-year-old woman on September 13 around Kota Bharu to assist with the investigation of the case. He said the incident began on September 12 when the victim received a phone call from an individual claiming to be a police officer from the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK).

items.title: Haze tightens its grip: 32 areas now recording unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Thirty-two areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30pm today, according to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal. Other areas with unhealthy API readings included Putrajaya (161), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (160), Shah Alam, Selangor (157), Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (156), and three areas in Johor - Segamat (156), Batu Pahat and Tangkak (155 each). Other affected areas were Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (147), Banting, Selangor (132), Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan (126), Alor Gajah, Melaka (119), Indera Mahkota Kuantan, Pahang (111), Kuala Selangor (108), Klang (107) and Balok Baru Kuantan in Pahang (103).

items.title: Police: Foreign man who caused disturbance at KLIA suspected of having mental health issues
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 20 — A Bangladeshi man who behaved aggressively and disturbed passengers at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 on Thursday is suspected of having mental health issues. KLIA district police chief ACP M. Ravi said the man had shouted loudly and disturbed passengers at an airline counter at KLIA Terminal 1 at 4.40pm. “Terminal security personnel who arrived to bring the situation under control took the suspect to the Terminal 1 police station for further action.

items.title: Cop’s knock wakes startled Audi driver before wrong-way scare in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 20 — A video posted on social media showing a car being driven against traffic on Jalan Jim Quee here has been traced to an Audi driver who is believed to have fallen asleep after finishing work. The knock woke the driver, Ng related, adding that the former then slowly moved the car forward into traffic. But possibly disoriented, the Audi driver was travelling against the flow of traffic towards Jalan Jim Quee.

items.title: Missing woman among two found dead in car in Durian Tunggal
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 20 — A man and a woman were found dead in a car at Taman Inang Sari, Durian Tunggal here around midnight last night. Alor Gajah district police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar said the bodies of the duo, aged 31 and 33, were discovered at 12.05am. “Initial checks found that the woman was the individual reported missing, while the man was believed to be her acquaintance,” he said.

items.title: Brother recounts failed attempt to pull mother to safety as grilles trap victims in Tambun fire
items.summary: Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad, 47, said his younger brother, Raja Muhammad Shukri, 30, had managed to reach their mother’s hand and tried to pull her to safety, but the grilles prevented him from getting her out of the house. The fire claimed the lives of their elderly parents, Zaitun Mohamed, 64, and Raja Ahmad Raja Ali, 70, as well as their nephew, Nik Abdurrahman Azimin Harith Helal, 18, in the two-storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun here. An elderly couple and their grandson were killed in a fire involving a two‑storey terraced house at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun in Ipoh early this morning.

items.title: PM channels RM5,000 initial assistance to Tambun fire victims
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today contributed RM5,000 in initial assistance to the family of the victims of a fire that claimed the lives of three family members at Persiaran Desa Tambun 4, Taman Desa Tambun, here early this morning. The contribution was presented by Tambun Member of Parliament’s (MP) special officer Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri, representing the Tambun MP’s Service Centre, to the family’s representative, Raja Ikhwan Hadi Raja Ahmad. Mohamad Hairul Amir said the assistance was an initial contribution to ease the burden on the family, which is now coping with the loss of three family members in the tragedy.

items.title: Technician killed after car skids into opposite lane and hits motorcycle in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 20 — A technician was killed after the motorcycle he was riding was hit by a car that lost control at Kilometre 70 of Jalan Jerangau-Jabor near Bukit Besi here this morning. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 7.30 am incident involved Mohd Yusop Abu Bakar, 34, who worked at a factory in Bukit Besi and was riding a Honda AFS110 motorcycle from Dungun towards Jerangau. “Initial investigations found that upon reaching the location, a Perodua Myvi driven by a 42-year-old man is believed to have lost control, skidded into the opposite lane and collided with the front of the victim’s motorcycle.

items.title: Malaysia to follow UN decision on any Malbatt deployment to Yemen, says defence minister
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Malaysia will be guided by any decision made by the United Nations (UN) should there be a proposal to deploy the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) peacekeeping force to Yemen amid the ongoing conflict there, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. Mohamed Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said Malaysia would not make such a decision unilaterally, stressing that any action must be based on a UN decision. “Malaysia’s decision will be guided by the decision made by the UN, rather than us acting on our own.

items.title: Fahmi: State‑specific political shifts may lead to Pakatan realignments, cooperation with Bersatu not discussed
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Sept 20 — The current political dynamics could lead to various political realignments, taking into account the unique political landscape of each state. Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said recent political developments could not be viewed through a single mould, as each state had its own unique political landscape and dynamics. He said this after officiating the Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) 2025 initiative of the Communications Ministry at Surau Kampung Tebat Kering, Kuala Pilah, here.

items.title: Floods: Five relief centres opened in Gua Musang, 221 evacuees housed
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 20 — Five temporary relief centres (PPS) have been opened in Gua Musang following heavy rain since last night, with 221 victims from 57 families housed at the centres as of 1.33pm today. The five relief centres are Masjid Jeram Tekoh, Jeram Tekoh Zone 3 Community Hall, Sekolah Kebangsaan Jeram Tekoh, Felda Chiku 6 Community Hall and Sekolah Kebangsaan Limau Kasturi 1. Meanwhile, Kelantan Civil Defence Force (APM) deputy director Lt Col Mohd Farid Ishak said the Gua Musang district APM had deployed personnel in two main teams to carry out follow-up operations in the affected areas.

items.title: ‘Whether Najib is released or not is a separate issue’: Khaled Nordin says King’s pardon prerogative should not be questioned
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today said any displeasure over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon should not extend to questioning the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s constitutional prerogative to grant them. Khaled said the granting of pardons was not unprecedented, with such decisions having been made in numerous cases involving individuals sentenced to death or life imprisonment, while the issue should also not be linked to ongoing efforts to unite Malay political parties. Khaled, who is also Kota Tinggi MP, said efforts towards Malay political unity were focused on safeguarding the community’s interests and political standing, and had nothing to do with Najib’s pardon.

items.title: ‘Lots of noise, then silence’: PAS’ Sanusi questions DAP’s Anthony Loke’s resignation offer over Najib house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — PAS election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today described the DAP’s decision to have only its secretary-general Anthony Loke offer to resign from the Cabinet over former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon as “firecracker politics”. Loke offered to resign as Transport Minister yesterday after a three-hour DAP central executive committee meeting, while the party decided its other ministers and deputy ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability. “DAP plays flip-flop politics.

items.title: DAP sec-gen’s Cabinet quit offer over Najib house arrest is his own call, says Umno veep Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 20 — Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister following former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon is entirely his own matter, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today. Loke offered to resign yesterday after DAP’s central executive committee meeting, saying the move was the party’s response to the decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, while other DAP ministers would remain in the unity government to maintain political stability. Khaled, who is also defence minister, said Loke’s resignation offer should not be confused with the decision involving Najib.

items.title: Sentul OCPD: Police to deploy mobile station near Najib’s Langgak Duta residence from tomorrow; Prisons Dept to handle monitoring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — A mobile police station will be deployed near a former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s official residence in Langgak Duta here from tomorrow to facilitate security arrangements during any transfer from prison to the residence. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the mobile police station was scheduled to be deployed at the residence from 7am tomorrow. “The mobile police station is not for the purpose of providing 24-hour security for Datuk Seri Najib.

items.title: MEF: RM1,000 Socso mobility allowance to improve job matching for workers relocating over 100km
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance for eligible Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributors is expected to improve the matching of workers with job opportunities, particularly where vacancies are located beyond their immediate areas. Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) Senior Adviser for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the initiative recognised that relocation and extended travel could involve significant upfront costs for workers to take jobs farther from home. However, Syed Hussain said MEF encouraged Socso to clearly communicate the eligibility criteria, application procedures and payment timelines to workers and employers.

items.title: Prisons Dept says still waiting for official notice before Najib’s house arrest can start
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s move from prison to house arrest has yet to get the formal green light from the Malaysian Prisons Department, which says it is still waiting for official written notification of the conditional pardon granted to the former prime minister. The Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon on Friday, allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of a RM50 million fine. “Any notification and official documents relating to the Pardons Board’s decision will be conveyed through the appropriate official channels before being submitted to the Malaysian Prisons Department for further action,” the department said in a statement today.

items.title: Education Ministry to revisit 2006 tuition centre ownership provisions, proposal goes to Cabinet next week
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 20 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will submit a proposal to review the ownership structure of tuition centres for Cabinet consideration next week. In a statement today, MOE said the provisions on tuition centre ownership were detailed in the Private Educational Institutions Policy Book published in 2006. “MOE takes note of the various views raised regarding the provisions and is always open to hearing the views of all parties.

items.title: Sarawak agrees in principle to RM1.5b allocation for Sibu Economic Zone, deputy premier says
items.summary: SIBU, Sept 20 — The Sarawak government has agreed in principle to an initial RM1.5 billion allocation to establish the Sibu Economic Zone (SEZ) as a dedicated platform to coordinate and shape the city’s economic development. Also present was ACCCIS president Kong Chiong Ung. Dr Sim said ACCCIS and its affiliated chambers had over the years provided an important platform for business networking, policy dialogue, capacity building and engagement between the government and business community.

items.title: No one should feel obliged to help pay RM50m fine, Najib tells supporters as Umno solidarity fund hits RM1m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak says Malaysians who have offered to help pay the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon should not feel “burdened or obliged” to do so. The statement from his lawyers comes as the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund set up by Umno to help him meet the payment reached RM1 million by 9.30am yesterday, less than a day after it was launched. Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the fund collected RM165,645 within its first hour and RM634,562.02 within three hours, with many contributors giving RM10 or RM50.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution: Proposed House Arrest Act focuses on remand detainees and prison overcrowding
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 20 — The proposed House Arrest Act is aimed at addressing prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand detainees, who make up a significant proportion of the prison population while awaiting trial. Previously, I mooted introducing one specifically for remand detainees, as remand detainees are one of the causes of prison overcrowding,” he said in a video uploaded on his Facebook page today. “So, this combination of convicted inmates and remand detainees contributes to prison overcrowding.
